definition: means a cost sharing requirement under a health insurance policy that provides that the Policyholder / Insured will bear a specified percentage of the admissible claims amount. A co-payment does not reduce the Sum Insured.
plain: A share of every approved claim that you pay yourself, as a fixed percentage. If your policy has a 20% co-pay and the hospital bill is ₹1 lakh, the insurer pays ₹80,000 and you pay ₹20,000.
whyItMatters: A co-pay applies to every claim, forever — it is not a one-off excess. It is the most common reason a policy that looked cheap turns out not to be, and it is often attached quietly to senior-citizen plans and to cheaper variants of otherwise good ones. Check for it before you compare premiums, because a plan with a co-pay is not comparable to one without.
